cohort: 2766 mother-neonate pairs with full-term, live-born neonates in the early neonatal period (<72 hours) with documented maternal pre-pregnancy and/or first-trimester BMI
finding: A direct relationship exists between maternal BMI and neonatal birth weight: underweight mothers had an increased risk of low birth weight neonates, while overweight and obese mothers were comparable to normal weight mothers for delivering macrosomic neonates.
mod_finding: Caesarean delivery was more prevalent in obese mothers (75.4%).
birth_weight: Mean birth weight increased with increasing maternal BMI
